shippingNews.postTitle: Polsteam Goplo, Polsteam’s Newest, Headed for Lakes

stories.body: The latest addition to the Polish Steamship fleet, the Polsteam Goplo, is in the St. Lawrence River headed for the Great Lakes. She left the port of Trois- Rivières on Friday. This is the last of a series of 12 identical LakerMax-class vessels built in Dalian, China, for the fleet. She loaded steel in South Korea (Incheon and Gwangyang) bound for Canadian ports, including Trois-Rivières, Hamilton, and Port Colborne. Polsteam Goplo Sept. 8 in Dalian. [Schulte Marine Concept] Rene Beauchamp

shippingNews.postTitle: Hull 3793 Exits Graving Dock at Sturgeon Bay Shipyard

stories.body: STURGEON BAY, WI – Discovert (Hull 3793), Bay Ship’s newest build, was pulled out of the large graving dock Friday thanks to the well-coordinated efforts of five tugs, including the G-tug Donald J. Sarter at the bow and Basic Towing’s Erika Kobasic at the stern. Notice her 70-foot tower and motion compensated gangway. She’s not sporting her final coat of paint yet. She’ll go back into the graving dock at some point. She is expected to begin her career next year as a service operation vessel for an offshore wind farm. Stewart J. shippingNews.postTitle: USCG Spar Back in Service at Duluth

stories.body: After a lengthy maintenance outage, Duluth-based USCGC Spar (WLB-206) departed Duluth Thursday afternoon on its autumn buoy (ATON) assignment. David Schauer – Shipping of the Lake Superior Region Duluth-based USCGC SPAR WLB-206 departed Thursday afternoon on its autumn buoy (ATON) assignment. In the distance the M/V Edwin H. Gott spins to head for Two Harbors where it will load ore from Minntac. [David Schauer]

stories.body: FRIDAY 5 p.m. UPDATE: Anglian Lady has gone to anchor in the Keweenaw waterway, probably for the night. There is no ETA as yet for Superior. ORIGINAL REPORT: SAULT STE. Marie, MI, around 5:30 p.m. Thursday with a destination of Fraser Shipyards, Superior, WI. She will tow the idled and damaged laker Michipicoten from Superior to the Purvis scrap dock on the Canadian side above the Soo Locks, where she will be dismantled. todayInHistory.title: NMGL Brings 2 Unique Great Lakes Stories to Life in New Exhibits
todayInHistory.text: TOLEDO, OH – The National Museum of the Great Lakes is bringing two unique Great Lakes stories to life this November with the opening of “An Artist at the Waters’ Edge: A Century of Marine Art” by Alexander Burns Cook on November 20, and the recently opened micro-exhibit “Model of the Armco: A Chief Engineer’s Handiwork.” Together, the exhibits offer visitors a look at the Great Lakes through the eyes of those who experienced, studied, and celebrated them. On display November 20 through February 14, 2027, “An Artist at the Waters’ Edge” explores the remarkable life and artwork of Alexander Burns Cook, whose connection to the Great Lakes inspired nearly a century of artistic creativity. From childhood adventures along the St. Joseph River and sailing Lake Michigan with his father to sketching commercial freighters entering Cleveland Harbor, Cook developed a lifelong appreciation for the region’s waterways and working vessels. An editorial cartoonist for The Cleveland Plain Dealer, art educator, and accomplished marine artist, Cook captured the character of the Great Lakes through illustrations, paintings, and sketches. He was also a longtime board member, volunteer curator, and dedicated supporter of the Great Lakes Historical Society and its National Museum of the Great Lakes. For 54 years, Cook donated original artwork for the organization’s annual Christmas cards, sharing his artistic talents and love of the Lakes with generations of supporters. todayInHistory.title: Life Aboard the Edmund Fitzgerald Described in Letters from Cadet
todayInHistory.text: David "Cowboy" Weiss in 1974. [GLSHS] DETROIT, MI – It wasn't just the hat that earned Edmund Fitzgerald crew member David Weiss his nickname "Cowboy." It was his friend and Great Lakes Maritime Academy classmate David James, who had just watched Frank Zappa's 1971 movie "200 Motels" featuring the character Lonesome Cowboy Burt. When James saw Weiss standing outside a classroom dressed in black and wearing a cowboy hat, the nickname came easily."He looked a little different," James said. Weiss was less "bummy" than the rest of their classmates, who dressed to emulate the sailors they were training to join. The day they met, James gave Weiss his nickname "Cowboy Burt." DuMouchelles auction house in downtown Detroit is selling letters written by a man killed in the Edmund Fitzgerald sinking in Lake Superior on Nov. 10, 1975. The letters were written by David Weiss while he was on the Fitzgerald. The friendship between Weiss and James is chronicled in a series of letters they exchanged while out on the inland seas in 1975, when Weiss was on the Edmund Fitzgerald and James on the Walter A. Sterling. The last was sent Oct. 30, about two weeks before Weiss went down with the Edmund Fitzgerald during a storm in Lake Superior. Twenty-eight crewmates perished along with him. marineWeather.synopsis: A 29.6 inch low is crossing James Bay while a 30.3 inch high is departing to the east over the Atlantic, causing a SW-NE pressure gradient across Lake Superior between 29.7 and 29.9 inches. This gradient remains much of today as the low shifts northeast, becoming a more uniform 29.9 inches by tonight. Pressure falls to 29.7 inches Sunday as a cold front tracks across the lake and a second low develops. The low lifts northeast by late Sunday, and pressure rises to 30.2 inches by early Monday as high pressure at 30.5 inches approaches from the southern Canadian Prairies. This high pressure shifts southeast toward the Upper Great Lakes and builds to 30.6 inches into Wednesday, sending pressure to 30.5 inches over Lake Superior Tuesday into Wednesday. As low moves east on Thursday, pressure diminishes slightly to 30.4 inches.

Low pressure around 29.5 inches over James Bay will move across northern Quebec today into tonight. This will maintain breezy south winds across the lake. A cold front will move eastward across the lake Sunday morning, bringing a gusty northwest shift by the afternoon. A few gale force gusts may occur over southern portions of the lake Sunday afternoon. Northwest winds will remain brisk behind the front into Monday night, as strong high pressure around 30.6 inches moves into the northern Plains. Winds will taper off Tuesday into Wednesday, as the high moves across the region.
High pressure, 30.40 inches, over Appalachians today will support seasonably warm and moderate southerly winds over the weekend.

A ridge averaging 30.20 inches will gradually weaken to 30.00 inches through Sunday. A cold front 29.90 inches will move east across Lake Erie Sunday night. Another ridge averaging 30.40 inches will build behind the front by early next week.

A ridge averaging 30.4 inches will continue to affect the lake through Sunday as the embedded high pressure center persists over the Mid Atlantic states this morning, before moving northeastward toward New England and then to the Atlantic waters near Nova Scotia today through Sunday. The ridge exits east allowing a cold front to sweep eastward across the lake Sunday night. Behind the front, another ridge averaging 30.5 inches across the northern Great Plains on Monday, will build east across the entire Great Lakes region through Tuesday. This now 30.7 inch surface high pressure is expected to move east of the region Wednesday.
